intake_stage_mapping.realization: XYZ bond inference, chemistry tags/charges, atom/bond/triplet/quadruplet motifs and corrected fixed packing
Per-subtype mean/sample-standard-deviation scaling, not a distributional Gaussian guarantee
Thirteen full configured graph transformers, not SchNet
Distance-biased multi-head attention across typed motifs with grouped subtype prediction heads
Six-decimal unscaled predictions, fixed coupling-specific model masks and central-five mean, no LightGBM

limitations: Automated Tier 3 Community reconstruction. No Tier 1 human certification or Tier 2 usage qualification; original inaccurate intake remains draft.

Pinned Bosch graph-transformer solution corrects the intake SchNet/LightGBM claims. All thirteen full configurations are retained; no original pretrained checkpoint or historical accuracy parity is claimed.

Explicit corrected triplet packing/model indices and chunked evaluation; modern OpenBabel/pandas interfaces. Caller-seeded batching and complete structured checkpoints replace launcher global state and model pickles.

Original chemistry requires supported connected motifs and fixed 29/406/54/117 capacities. Degenerate or absent motifs, unsupported chemistry, out-of-vocabulary labels and nonfinite scaling can fail. This is not a general molecular chemistry predictor.

Original per-record bond corrections are excluded. Optional manual corrections in lower-level preprocessing are not exposed in this version of the pipeline payload; original-record parity is not claimed.

Fitted vocabulary/scaling precede the source population split. This preserves source behavior rather than claiming leakage-free validation. The eight supervised primary type slots are explicitly reserved for smaller populations.

Source inverse-square-root schedule is initialized but never advanced after warmup; this behavior is preserved. Original quadruplet cutout and chunked log-type-loss training combinations remain unsupported.

Graph evidence uses one explicitly configured synthetic SGD epoch for every full model. Sixteen stochastic optimizer/scheduler resume combinations and validation selection controls were checked separately with analytic synthetic inputs, not historical training runs.
Validation selection requires all eight finite type metrics. Full-population mode retains the last epoch; finite aggregate MAE alone is not represented as complete competition macro-metric coverage.

Per-model prediction rounding to six decimals precedes the coupling-specific central-five ensemble, matching original CSV precision. Opaque caller IDs are remapped to exactly representable internal float32 integers.

CPU execution requires locally provisioned hash-verified software and pinned dependencies in the matcher environment. No downloads, GPU/mixed-precision qualification, clean-environment installation or resource-cap guarantee is claimed.
Geometry, fitted state, checkpoints, training outputs and predictions are private runtime data. Publication evidence contains synthetic fixtures and aggregate checks only.
The new graph executes all thirteen full configured models for one explicitly requested synthetic SGD epoch each; historical training-duration and accuracy parity remain unproven.
Current execution uses NumPy 2.2.6, recorded in the new immutable report; it does not overwrite the earlier NumPy 2.4.2 qualification.
The complete training body is unchanged apart from moving final ensemble selection/reduction into explicit graph boundaries.
Central rank mean is domain independent. Molecular identity, model masks and retained count stay in recipe policy.
Dictionary shape and identity checks do not independently authenticate training provenance.
Provider eligibility and corrected-original publication require separate transactional qualification.
Automated Tier 3 only; no Tier 1 human certification or Tier 2 usage qualification.
Central rank mean is domain independent. The recipe supplies model selection and retained count through explicit graph edges.
Synthetic training qualification does not establish competition accuracy, historical trained-weight parity or independent-run tensor identity.
Installed package hashes were checked against their own RECORD files, not independently authenticated publisher signatures. Clean deployment qualification is not claimed.
Validation bounds native and Torch thread pools to one; deployment must configure its own resource limits.
Pinned public Bosch software is a runtime dependency. Original pretrained checkpoint parity is not claimed.
Software dependencies are separate from registered atom dependencies. This review alone does not approve catalog records.

Qualified with NumPy 2.2.6. Installed files were checked against their own RECORD; clean deployment and independent publisher authentication are not claimed.

Two-dimensional NumPy array with at least one row and real integer/unsigned/floating dtype; reject booleans, complex, objects and nonfinite inputs. Retained is a Python int in [1, rows], excluding bool and NumPy scalar integers. Convert to a fresh column-contiguous float64 matrix, sort ascending per column, and apply NumPy mean to the slice starting at floor((rows-retained)/2) with exactly retained rows. Odd discarded counts remove one more upper-tail observation. Reject float64 conversion or reduction overflow, including intermediate sum overflow. Zero columns yield an empty float64 vector. No category, identity, model count, retained count, normalization or units are prescribed.
